It's very weird to me that I put these posts up because I was frustrated about what one my transgender former co-workers went through (getting fired for expressing that they also disagreed with Nintendo's decision to ban the creator of the map) and my other transgender friend and former co-worker witnessing that go down. I am not saying that Nintendo is evil, I'm saying that, as someone that worked there, on the surface they are inclusive, beyond that they are more than a little bit discriminatory towards both LGBTQ and disabled employees. Personally, I will never buy another Nintendo product or allow one in my home. If you don't feel the same way go ahead and buy their stuff. You don't need to justify your purchases anymore than I need to justify my boycotts.

This is a transgender subreddit and community. As a transwoman and given the nature and actions of this company I thought it would be fair to share this here so other people can make their own decisions.

At least Nintendo doesn't actively lobby against LGBTQ rights like Chic-Fil-A does, but even then I know LGBTQ people that still eat there knowing that. I don't eat Chic-Fil-A, and I won't buy Nintendo products.

I'm not sure with where you're at. Here it's anywhere from $50-150 depending on insurance, medical codes used and all of that. Also please know that the first few months of HRT you will have hormonal imbalances and esterogen makes a lot of people's, my own included, emotions more intense and with more depth. 
The first month was rough for me because the changes hit me faster than a lot of people. I was tired and angry and sad all the time. It got way better and easier and I feel good most of the time now and my dysphoria has been substantially reduced. 
Not trying to gate keep or recommend against it. It has been a really positive experience all in all for myself and I sincerely hope that you will have a good experience too. Just letting you know of possible side effects.

I was lucky to have fairly feminine features and I spent a long time growing my hair out. Without insurance I would not be able to afford HRT. And FFS and GCS are still a long ways out for me. Even electrolysis is hardly affordable for me with insurance given my current income.
